Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘one arrowhead pierces three checkpoints.’ In Qinshan Wensui's exchange, Juliang asks what it is like when one arrow pierces three checkpoints; Qinshan answers, ‘release the master within the checkpoints and let me see.’ After Juliang calls it a good arrow shot in the wrong place, Qinshan seizes him and says to set piercing three checkpoints aside and shoot an arrow for Qinshan; Juliang hesitates and is struck seven times. Yunmen gives the whole phrase as his own answer after asking how to undertake ‘covering heaven and earth, weighing the coming mechanism to the fraction’ without involving worldly conditions and receiving no answer from the assembly. Later teaching-seat records take up the same archery line with staffs, calling it a flash-like edge, and verse uses it as a closing line. The Zen bend is the military checkpoint-and-arrow formula's repeated use as an answer, challenge, and teaching-seat line in public encounter. The records do not define a universal set of three checkpoints here, so this entry does not substitute Huanglong's or Doushuai's named threes.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense: the literal question, answer-line, and later quotation all name the same arrow/checkpoint event. The distinct Huanglong and Doushuai taxonomies belong under “three barriers” (三關) and are not silently read into this formula.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一鏃破三關時如何？師曰：放出關中主看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Juliang asks the formula as a public question; Qinshan asks to see the master inside the checkpoints.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一鏃破三關即且置，試為欽山發箭看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Qinshan sets the formula aside and demands an arrow shot for himself.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不涉世緣，作麼生承當？眾無對。自代曰：一鏃破三關。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yunmen supplies the phrase as his own answer when the assembly gives none.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一鏃破三關，機鋒如掣電。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷). Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Wanshan Zhengning as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.
